pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is poetry important in our daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication
2. appreciate poetry for self- expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY
This lesson teaches Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry for Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate poetry for self- expression
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry above.
2. Explain Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is poetry important in our daily life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication
2. appreciate poetry for self- expression

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
